8607.t: BM2719: Bio-Heat and Mass Transfer Laboratory
8607.b:
Course Details

Subject {L-T-P / C} : BM2719 : Bio-Heat and Mass Transfer Laboratory { 0-0-3 / 2}

Subject Nature : Practical

Syllabus

Module 1 :

1. Determination of total thermal conductivity of composite walls
2. Determination of critical radius of insulating material
3. Determination Stefan Boltzmann’s constant of radiant heat transfer
4. Determination of the Biot number and the heat transfer coefficient
5. Determination of the influence of thermal conductivity and ambient temperature on thermal distribution in biological tissues
6. Investigation of heat and mass transfer characteristics during laser cutting and laser engraving
7. Determination of overall co-efficient and the effectiveness of Heat Exchanger
8. Computational heat transfer analysis of the steady-state temperature distribution of a composite wall
9. Analysis of the steady state thermal conduction of composite wall
10. Transient thermal heat analysis of a bar in the stagnant air using convection boundary condition

Course Objective

1 .

To understand the principles of heat and mass transfer as apply to biological systems, including conduction, convection, radiation processes
2 .

To analyze heat transfer coefficients and unsteady state heat transfer phenomena in biological systems and solve real-world problems in biomedical engineering
3 .

To enhance skills to assess heat and mass transfer phenomena in biological systems
4 .

To investigate computational techniques for steady-state and transient heat transfer analysis using ANSYS

Course Outcome

1 .

After completing the course, the student will be able to
1 Apply heat transfer principles to determine thermal conductivity, critical radius, and radiation constants in composite systems
2 Evaluate heat transfer coefficients and thermal distribution in biological tissues using unsteady state analysis
3 Assess heat and mass transfer characteristics in laser processing for heat exchanger design
4 Analyze the performance of heat exchangers using overall heat transfer coefficient and effectiveness metrics
5 Analyze steady-state and transient heat transfer problems using computational tools like ANSYS

Essential Reading

1 .

Theodore and Lavine, Fundamentals of Heat and Mass Transfer, Wiley , (8th ed), 2017

Course Details

Subject {L-T-P / C} : BM6633 : Advanced Environmental Biotechnology { 3-0-0 / 3}

Subject Nature : Theory

Syllabus

Module 1 :

Module 1: Fundamentals of Environmental Biotechnology
Introduction to Environmental Biotechnology, Basics of microbial growth and metabolism, Enzyme kinetics and regulation, Overview of respiration and energy generation, Ethical issues in environmental biotechnology
Module 2: Molecular Tools for Biodiversity and Community Dynamics
Biodiversity analysis and its significance, Community dynamics and ecological interactions, Amplified Ribosomal DNA Restriction Analysis (ARDRA), Restriction Fragment Length Polymorphism (RFLP), Denaturing Gradient Gel Electrophoresis (DGGE), Temperature Gradient Gel Electrophoresis (TGGE)

Introduction to Metagenomics, Next Generation Sequencing Technology, Microbial transformation reactions: aerobic and anaerobic biotransformation, Bioremediation technology and influencing factors, Microbial detoxification of organic pollutants and endocrine disruptors (insecticides, herbicides, fungicides, polychlorinated biphenyls, heavy metals)

Environmental monitoring techniques, Bioreporters, biomarkers, and biosensors, Quorum sensing technology, Biological energy and biomass production from waste, Wastewater treatment methods, Activated sludge treatment process, Sustainable waste management practices

Environmental impact assessment techniques, Genetically Modified Organisms (GMOs) and biosafety, Ethical issues in environmental biotechnology, Case studies on the application of environmental biotechnology in industry and research

To provide postgraduate biotechnology students with a comprehensive understanding of the fundamental principles of environmental biotechnology
2 .

To equip students with the knowledge and skills to utilize molecular tools and advanced techniques in environmental contexts

To prepare students to apply biotechnological strategies for addressing sustainability challenges in environmental contexts

Course Outcome

1 .

Apply biotechnology concepts to real-world challenges.
Utilizing molecular techniques for microbial biodiversity analysis.
Conduct investigations using metagenomics and sequencing technologies.
Develop projects for environmental monitoring and detoxifying emerging pollutants.

Subject {L-T-P / C} : EE6315 : Industrial Automation and Control { 3-0-0 / 3}

Subject Nature : Theory

Syllabus

Module 1 :

Introduction: [2L]
The architecture of Industrial Automation Systems, Automation: current and future scenarios, and the Industry 4.0 paradigm.
Module 2 :

Sensing and Measurement Systems: [15L]
Measurement Systems Characteristics, Errors and Calibration
Displacement and Speed Measurement: Potentiometer, LVDT, Proximity sensor, Optical speed measurement,
Temperature Measurement: RTD, Thermocouple,
Pressure, Force and Torque Measurement: Diaphragms, Bellows, Bourdon Tube, Strain gauge, Load shell
Flow Measurement: Obstruction type flowmeters, Electromagnetic Flowmeter, Turbine type Flowmeter, Vortex type Flowmeter, Ultrasonic Flowmeter

Signal conditioning circuits: Unbalanced D.C./ A.C. Bridge, with Push-Pull configuration, Capacitance Amplifier, Differential Amplifier and Instrumentation Amplifier, Transmitters.

Automatic Controllers: [16L]
PID Controller: Control Algorithms, Implementation and Tuning
Special Control Structures: Feedforward, Ratio
Introduction to Sequence Control: The Programmable Logic Controller (PLC): PLC hardware environment, RLL, Scan Cycle, RLL Programs, RLL Elements: Timer, counter, etc., case studies.
Supervisory level Controllers: DCS and SCADA
Module 5 :

Industrial Communication Technologies and Protocols: [2L]
Networking of Field Devices via FieldBus, ModBus, ProfiBus, etc.

1 .

This course aims to provide the students with a general view of the current trends, methods and tools offered by automation technologies. The course specifically focuses on architecture, components, and techniques for automation in industries.

Identify the role of automation systems for the industry

Summarize about various measurement and actuation techniques used in the industries

Understand the communication technologies and protocols for industrial systems
4 .

Analyze the role of different control techniques employed in process automation

Course Details

Subject {L-T-P / C} : PH5118 : Introduction to Soft Matter { 3-0-0 / 3}

Subject Nature : Theory

Syllabus

Module 1 :

(8 hrs) Introduction to soft matter. Properties of soft matter. Intermolecular Interactions. Short and long range forces. Structural organization of soft materials. Experimental techniques for investigating soft matter. Microscopy and scattering methods. Rheology. Response of matter to a shear stress.

Module 2 :

(8 hrs) Statistics of a random walk. Brownian motion and thermal fluctuation. Stokes-Einstein equation. Fick’s law. Phase transitions in soft matter, Liquid-liquid unmixing. Stable, metastable and unstable composition. Phase diagram of a liquid mixture.

Module 3 :

(8 hrs) Polymers. Polymer Chain Conformation. Ideal and Real chains. Scaling laws. Polymer solutions. Solvent Quality: Good, Bad and Theta. Gelation. Chemical gels. Physical gels. Percolation Model. Classical theory of gelation
Module 4 :

(8 hrs) Colloids. Types of Colloids. Characterization of Colloids. Stability of colloidal systems. Kinetic Stability. Thermodynamic Stability. Forces between Colloidal Particles. Van der Waals Forces. Electric Double-Layer Forces. Effect of polymers on colloid stability.
Module 5 :

(4 hrs) Amphiphiles. Surface Activity. Liquid Crystal. Characteristics and Identification Liquid Crystal Phases. Biological Soft Matter

Course Objective

1 .

To introduce students to the world of soft matter physics
2 .

To study the importance of random walk and statistical physics in explaining various soft matter phenomena.

3 .

To learn about the different types of polymers and gels based on various involved interactions.
4 .

To gain an understanding of the colloids and the underlying forces.

5 .

To provide basic ideas about amphiphiles, liquid crystals, and biological soft matter.

Course Outcome

1 .

CO 1: Students will understand the fundamental behaviour of soft matter.

2 .

CO2: Students will be able to use the statistical physics theory to build different theories and laws of soft matter.

3 .

CO3: Students will learn about polymer and gelation which will help them to understand its wide application in industry.

4 .

CO4: Students will gain knowledge about the characterization and stability of colloids.

5 .

CO5: Students will get a brief introduction to amphiphiles, liquid crystals, and biological soft matter.

Essential Reading

1 .

Ian W. Hamley, Introduction to Soft Matter: Synthetic and Biological Self-Assembling Materials, Wiley; Revised Edition (2007).

2 .

R. A. L. Jones, Soft Condensed Matter, Oxford University Press; First Edition (2002).

3 .

S. F. Sun, Physical Chemistry of Macromolecules: Basic Principles and Issues, Wiley; Second Edition (2004).

2 .

L. S. Hirst, Fundamentals of Soft Matter Science, CRC Press; Second Edition (2020).

3 .

M. Rubinstein and R. H. Colby, Polymer Physics, Oxford University Press; First Edition (2003)
